documents.title: Universal Guidelines for AI Use in Teaching and Learning: Course Syllabus Template Addendum
tiers: Permitted for Some Activities with Attribution
Permitted for All Activities with Attribution
documents.summary: A provost addendum asking faculty to promote ethical AI use and attribution, then to state a syllabus policy referencing the Academic Dishonesty Policy. It offers three template options from a full ban to open use with attribution, leaving the choice to each instructor.
documents.stance_why: The document sets no single rule: 'Faculty members have the flexibility to choose from the following options' (Not Permitted, Permitted for Some Activities with Attribution, Permitted for All Activities with Attribution), so it delegates and lists the tiers.

units.why: The preamble says faculty 'should promote ethical use of these tools' when bringing AI into teaching; it is a framework-level principle addressed to instructors, so P56 rather than a specific rule type.
units.anchor: faculty members at the university should promote ethical use of these tools
units.frag_start: When incorporating ChatGPT or any

units.why: 'This includes providing proper attribution when AI-generated content is used or presented' sets an attribution expectation for AI content; coded P24 (disclose) and addressed to all since it does not name who attributes.
units.anchor: providing proper attribution when AI-generated content is used or presented
units.frag_start: This includes providing proper attribution
units.policy: Proper attribution is provided when AI-generated content is used or presented.

units.why: Names the citation styles ('APA, IEEE, MLA') that AI citations follow; a citation-format rule, P24 since it names no tool, prompt or output details.
units.anchor: Citations should follow the guidelines specified by academic writing styles such as APA, IEEE, MLA
units.frag_start: Citations should follow the guidelines
units.frag_end: IEEE, MLA, or other relevant citation styles.
units.policy: Citations of AI-generated content follow academic writing style guidelines such as APA, IEEE, MLA, or other relevant styles.

units.why: States that faculty cannot always verify originality but 'can play a crucial role' educating students on originality; it asks instructors to explain integrity expectations, so P66.
units.anchor: play a crucial role with respect to educating student about the importance of originality
units.frag_start: While faculty members may not be able
units.policy: Faculty play a crucial role in educating students about the importance of originality in their work and in upholding university values related to academic integrity.

units.why: Faculty are 'encouraged to explore alternative assessment approaches' because of AI; assessment redesign, P35, with a soft modality (encouraged = should).
units.anchor: encouraged to explore alternative assessment approaches
units.frag_start: Faculty members are encouraged to explore
units.frag_end: identification of AI-generated content when necessary.
units.policy: Faculty members are encouraged to explore alternative assessment approaches.

units.why: Faculty are encouraged to use 'technology tools that ... facilitate the identification of AI-generated content'; this endorses detection tools as a means of identifying misuse (P40), not a rejection of detectors.
units.anchor: technology tools that promote academic integrity and facilitate the identification of AI-generated content
units.frag_start: Faculty members are encouraged to explore
units.frag_end: identification of AI-generated content when necessary.
units.policy: Faculty members are encouraged to explore technology tools that promote academic integrity and facilitate the identification of AI-generated content when necessary.

units.why: 'It is essential for faculty members and students to be aware of the licensing agreements and terms of service' of AI tools: licensing/terms awareness, P52.
units.anchor: aware of the licensing agreements and terms of service associated with the use of AI
units.frag_start: It is essential for faculty members and
units.policy: Faculty members and students are aware of the licensing agreements and terms of service associated with the use of AI language models.

units.why: Faculty are 'encouraged to refer to official documentation provided by the language model's developers'; a pointer to terms/usage restrictions, so P52 (licensing and terms).
units.anchor: encouraged to refer to official documentation provided by the language model's developers
units.frag_start: Faculty members are encouraged to refer
units.policy: Faculty members are encouraged to refer to official documentation provided by the language model's developers and relevant platform-specific guidelines.

units.why: 'compliance with ethical and legal guidelines is crucial' states that AI use must follow legal and ethical rules; P77 fits better than P56 because it is about complying with law and terms.
units.anchor: compliance with ethical and legal guidelines is crucial
units.frag_start: Different language models may have varying
units.policy: Compliance with ethical and legal guidelines is crucial when using AI language models.

units.why: 'Standards specific to the dissemination of scholarly products in various venues are likewise essential (conferences, journals)': defers to venue rules for scholarship, P62.
units.anchor: Standards specific to the dissemination of scholarly products in various venues are likewise essential
units.frag_start: Standards specific to the dissemination
units.policy: Standards specific to the dissemination of scholarly products in various venues (conferences, journals, etc) are essential.

units.why: 'the policy in the syllabus should be explicitly stated' requires each syllabus to state an AI policy, referencing the Academic Dishonesty Policy: P09.

units.policy: The AI policy in the syllabus is explicitly stated with reference to the university Academic Dishonesty Policy.

units.why: 'Faculty members have the flexibility to choose from the following options' hands the choice to instructors per course: P04.

units.why: Offers three named syllabus options ('Not Permitted', 'Permitted for Some Activities with Attribution', 'Permitted for All Activities with Attribution'): a tier template, P05.
units.anchor: Permitted for Some Activities with Attribution
units.frag_start: Not Permitted:
units.policy: The university provides three syllabus options for AI use: Not Permitted; Permitted for Some Activities with Attribution; Permitted for All Activities with Attribution.

units.why: Option 'Not Permitted' says AI assistance 'is not allowed for any activities or assignments' and AI content 'strictly prohibited': a blanket default ban in the course, P01.
units.anchor: is not allowed for any activities or assignments
units.frag_start: Assistance from large language model and
units.policy: Under the Not Permitted option, assistance from large language models and other generative AI is not allowed for any activities or assignments, and the use of AI-generated content is strictly prohibited.

units.why: 'All submissions must be the original work of the student' makes students own submitted work; P29 within the Not Permitted option.

units.why: 'Possible disciplinary action ... is described in the university's Academic Dishonesty Policy' classifies violations as academic dishonesty handled by that process: P36 (no specific penalty, so not P37). Coded once; the same sentence recurs in the other options.
units.anchor: Possible disciplinary action for violations of this course policy
units.frag_start: Possible disciplinary action for violations of
units.policy: Possible disciplinary action for violations of the course AI policy is described in the university's Academic Dishonesty Policy.

units.why: Option 2 allows AI 'only for specified activities or assignments': narrow permitted uses set per assignment, P04 over P05 since the tiers were already coded.

units.policy: Under the Permitted for Some Activities option, the use of large language models and other generative AI is allowed only for specified activities or assignments, with proper attribution.

units.policy: Students clearly indicate when AI-generated content has been used.

units.policy: Students cite the specific language model and platform employed, following APA, MLA or another relevant academic citation style.

units.policy: Under the Permitted for All Activities option, use of large language models and other generative AI is permitted for all activities and assignments, but proper attribution is required.

units.why: Option 3: students 'should acknowledge the use of AI-generated content and provide appropriate citations': disclosure, P24 (similar wording to option 2 but a separate option).

units.policy: Students acknowledge the use of AI-generated content and provide appropriate citations following APA, MLA, or another relevant academic style.

units.why: 'students are expected to engage critically and creatively with the material' even with AI help: students remain the primary thinker, P32.
